title: Modification label sensors sans effet (renaming a sensor label in System Monitor widget settings has no effect)
line: Renaming a sensor with the pencil in a System Monitor widget's Sensors Details page now shows the new name right away
explanation: In Sensors Details, the pencil handlers changed the label inside the existing cfg_sensorLabels object and then emitted its change signal by hand. The sensor chips read their labels from that same object, so their binding never saw a new value and the chip kept showing the old name, although the label was stored and Apply became enabled. The change assigns a new object (a copy with the edited label) in the three handlers, so the chips update. This is exactly Niccolò's open MR 503, applied unchanged.

commits.message:
faces/ConfigSensors: show the new label after renaming a sensor

Renaming a sensor with the pencil in Sensors Details kept showing the
old name, because the label was changed inside the existing object and
the chip never saw a new value. Assign a new object with the new label.

BUG: 527464

media.caption: Pure master: after renaming 'Used Physical Memory' to 'RAM used' and pressing the check button, the chip still shows 'Used Physical Memory' (Apply is enabled)
With the fix: the same steps leave the chip showing 'RAM used'
With the fix, after renaming all three sensors and OK: the widget shows the new labels

reviews.text: Solid, idiomatic QML fix in libksysguard's ConfigSensors.qml that replaces in-place mutation of cfg_sensorLabels with Object.assign({}, root.cfg_sensorLabels, {[sensorId]: label}) across all three Faces.Choices handlers. Assigning a new JS object ensures Choices.labels actually changes and triggers the sensor chip text bindings immediately while preserving Apply state and config persistence. The screenshots, multi-sensor rename checks, and passing 9/9 autotests verify the fix cleanly.

Right cause and layer: the three onSensorLabelChanged handlers mutated cfg_sensorLabels in place and emitted the change signal by hand, so the chips bound to `labels: root.cfg_sensorLabels` kept the same object and never refreshed. Assigning a fresh Object.assign copy is the idiomatic QML fix, keeps configurationChanged()/Apply working, and the screenshots show the chip and the widget body with the new labels after OK, matching the reporter's 'label not modified on validation'. Nits: the before shot comes from a differently titled dialog ('System Monitor Settings', white colour swatch) than the after shots ('Memory Usage Settings'), so the pair isn't a strict same-widget comparison; the colour handlers' identical in-place pattern could get the same treatment in a follow-up.
